beats.text: It was never meant to be JavaScript.
beats.note: Brendan Eich used the name Mocha for his prototype in early to mid May 1995. It shipped as LiveScript in a September 1995 beta, then became JavaScript for the December release.

beats.text: Management said it must look like Java.
beats.note: Netscape was negotiating with Sun to include Java in Navigator. Eich has called the Java influences unfortunate, and says the two languages served different audiences.

beats.text: Eich called the name a marketing ploy.
beats.note: According to Wikipedia, he considered the JavaScript name a marketing ploy by Netscape, at a time when Java was popular.
Java and JavaScript are similar in name and syntax but differ greatly in design. MDN is blunt about it: JavaScript is not interpreted Java.

beats.name: JavaScript
beats.role: The first appearance date Wikipedia gives for the language under its new name.

beats.name: Sun Microsystems
beats.role: The JavaScript trademark was originally issued to Sun. It moved to Oracle in 2009.

beats.text: Mocha, LiveScript, JavaScript. Three names in one year.
